questions.questionText: Which statement about factors of production is correct?

options.text: The fruit picked from the tree is called land.
The managers of a company are called enterprise.
The money used to finance a project is called capital.
The owner of a company is called labour.

questions.questionText:
A person can make 10 items to sell on a craft stall in a day.
What is the opportunity cost if the person decides to paint a picture instead?

options.text: 10 craft items
the cost of the materials for the craft items
the cost of the paint for the picture
the value of the picture

questions.questionText:
The diagram shows the demand for chocolate.
price
quantity demanded
per week
What could cause the movement from point X to point Y?

options.text: a change in tastes
a fall in the price of chocolate
an increase in income
a successful advertising campaign for chocolate

questions.questionText:
A company produces an electric car that can be driven much further than other electric cars
without needing recharging. The car does not emit the dangerous fumes that petrol cars do. The
batteries that power the car are very expensive and the company is building a huge factory to
produce batteries more cheaply.
Which concepts can be applied to the above statement?

options.text: average cost and mergers
external costs and mixed economy
private costs and economies of scale
public sector and market failure

questions.questionText:
People often eat biscuits when they drink a cup of tea. Between 2010 and 2015, the consumption
of sweet biscuits decreased because of health warnings about high sugar consumption. Sales of
tea, as a result, also fell.
How would this be shown on demand and supply diagrams for biscuits and tea?
biscuits tea

options.text: demand curve moves to left demand curve moves to left
demand curve moves to right demand curve moves to right
movement down along the demand curve demand curve moves to right
movement up along the demand curve demand curve moves to left

questions.questionText:
A student needs to borrow $60000 to pay for a five-year university course in medicine.
What would motivate the student to borrow to pay for the course?

options.text: Debts must be repaid within the first five years of work.
Further training in hospitals must follow graduation.
High earnings are expected in the long-run.
Many skills gained on the course are non-transferable.

questions.questionText:
The Congress of South African Trade Unions (COSATU) is the biggest union federation in South
Africa. It represents public sector workers.
In 2010, it had an increase in membership. In the same year, COSATU’s bargaining strength
declined.
What could explain this?

options.text: There was an increase in government spending on welfare payments.
There was an increase in the country’s unemployment rate.
There was an increase in the geographical mobility of labour.
There was an increase in union funds.

questions.questionText: Which worker is most likely to risk facing a falling income towards the end of their career?

options.text: a manager in an engineering firm
a manual worker in a building firm
a supervisor in a retail firm
an office worker in an advertising firm

questions.questionText: What is the most likely reason why airline pilots earn more than agricultural workers?

options.text: Agricultural work is difficult.
Pilots work regular hours.
There is a surplus of agricultural workers.
There is no shortage of pilots.

questions.questionText: To achieve horizontal integration, a firm producing tyres could merge with another firm producing

options.text: motor cars.
rubber.
tyre-producing machinery.
tyres.

questions.questionText:
A car manufacturer has a highly mechanised assembly line using robots and a few skilled
workers. An international exam board employs many thousands of examiners to mark candidates’
examination papers.
Which row describes each of these activities?
car manufacturer international exam board

options.text: capital-intensive capital-intensive
capital-intensive labour-intensive
labour-intensive capital-intensive
labour-intensive labour-intensive

questions.questionText:
A monopoly takes over an industry from competitive firms.
What is not likely to be true about a monopoly compared with a competitive firm?

options.text: A monopoly will earn a higher rate of profit.
A monopoly will gain a greater share of the market.
A monopoly will offer a wider choice to the consumer.
A monopoly will operate on a larger scale of production.

questions.questionText:
2 3 1 4
Who has the most elastic demand for t-shirts when the price rises from $10 to $15?

options.text: Elsa
George
Hamid
Shara

questions.questionText: When is a tax progressive?

options.text: when some goods have a higher tax than others
when the rate of tax increases as income increases
when the tax is linked to the rate of inflation
when the tax is on incomes rather than on goods or services

questions.questionText: Why can government spending be described both as a fiscal policy and a supply-side policy?

options.text: It has a nationwide effect and can control firms’ production possibility curves.
It is announced in the budget and can increase the economy’s ability to produce.
It is determined by the central bank and can raise the cost of production of firms.
It must equal tax revenue and can regulate the amount of the money supply.

questions.questionText:
In trying to achieve one of its aims a government may make it difficult to achieve another aim.
What is an example of this conflict?

options.text: Achieving a more even distribution of income may prevent a rise in the average standard of living.
Achieving an increase in economic growth may prevent full employment.
Achieving full employment may prevent stable prices.
Achieving stable prices may prevent a current account surplus on the balance of payments.

questions.questionText:
A government cuts the rate of income tax.
What effect is this likely to have on tax evasion and revenue from indirect taxes?
revenue from
tax evasion
indirect taxes

options.text: decrease increase
decrease no effect
increase increase
increase no effect

questions.questionText:
A newspaper reported that a country’s economy had grown by 3% during the last year.
What must have increased in that year?

options.text: costs of production
gross domestic product
unemployment
wage levels

questions.questionText:
In the poorest developing countries it is difficult to measure the size of GDP.
What is the main cause of this?

options.text: A high proportion of the paid workforce is in the informal sector.
Employment in rural areas is seasonal in nature.
The provision of services cannot be given a value.
Women are discriminated against in many jobs.

questions.questionText:
The information below refers to an economy for a financial year.
government expenditure = $2866 million
government revenue = $1940 million
What was the budget balance of the government in that year?

options.text: $926 million in deficit
$4806 million in deficit
$926 million in surplus
$4806 million in surplus

questions.questionText: What is likely to show that a country has a rising level of economic development?

options.text: a reduced inflation rate
a reduced national income per head
a reduced provision of healthcare (merit good)
a reduced unemployment rate

questions.questionText:
A government in a developing country has given extra funds to promote trade in rural areas by
encouraging the establishment of small shops.
What is likely to increase as a result?

options.text: primary industry in the private sector
primary industry in the public sector
secondary industry in the public sector
tertiary industry in the private sector

questions.questionText: Which government policy is most likely to increase the volume of exports?

options.text: devaluation
embargoes
quotas
tariffs

questions.questionText: Which method would both reduce imports and encourage exports?

options.text: embargoes on dangerous products
quotas on agricultural produce
subsidies on locally-produced electronics
tariffs on iron and steel products

questions.questionText:
The currency exchange rate of the South African rand for the Botswana pula fell by 5.7%
between August 2014 and August 2015.
What would be the immediate effect of this?

options.text: Botswana’s level of protection would fall.
Botswana’s tourists travelling to South Africa would find it less expensive.
South Africa’s imports would be cheaper.
South Africa’s tourists travelling to Botswana would receive more pula per rand.

questions.questionText:
In 2015, China was the world’s biggest importer of oil. In August 2015, China devalued its
currency.
What is likely to have happened?

options.text: The price of China’s exports fell and world oil prices rose as China’s demand decreased.
The price of China’s exports rose and world oil prices fell as China’s demand increased.
The price of China’s imports fell and world oil prices rose as China’s demand increased.

The price of China’s imports rose and world oil prices fell as China’s demand decreased.
